views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the Section 301 tariff list in reserve and continue talks rather than firing or folding. Send Ross to lock specific agriculture and energy purchase volumes, but treat those as a down payment, not a settlement. Do not lift the ZTE denial order except for a law-enforcement package (fines, board/management change, compliance) that is independent of the trade communique, and do not accept a purchase-only deal that leaves forced tech transfer, cyber theft, and IP theft unaddressed.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a modest opportunity, not a crisis. The U.S. opened this file (301 investigation Aug 2017; 301 findings and tariff directive Mar 22; ~$50B list Apr 3) from a strong domestic position: consumer sentiment ~98, industrial production still expanding, VIX back to 12.58, and goods trade deficit actually narrowing to -$66.6B. China has already blinked toward talks and a "significantly increase" purchase pledge after mirroring the $50B list and hitting ~$3B of U.S. farm goods over 232. That is leverage, not existential risk. The threat is not more negative because the May 19 joint statement is non-binding (no $200B figure; IP language is only that China will "advance relevant amendments"), Lighthizer publicly said purchases are secondary to structural tech issues and reserved tariffs/investment restrictions/export controls, and China's proposed soy/auto/aircraft list remains a farm-belt and Boeing exposure if talks fail. Escalating now would waste a ceasefire markets already priced (Mnuchin: trade war "on hold"; tariffs can be put back on). Conceding now would cash out the 301/ZTE pressure for a vague shopping list—exactly the outcome Lighthizer, Schumer, and the 301 record warn against. Negotiate with the list live and ZTE treated as enforcement, not a trade chip.
key_factors: May 19 joint statement is a vague purchase framework, not a structural deal
301 $50B list and ZTE denial order remain unused/unresolved leverage
U.S. macro is healthy; dispute not yet biting GDP, sentiment, or vol
China's live soy/auto/aircraft retaliation list is the main U.S. downside if talks collapse
Internal U.S. split: Mnuchin/Kudlow pause vs Lighthizer insistence on IP/tech transfer

sources_cited.excerpt: US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold." Markets rally.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine, and related items) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment latest 98 (May 2018), still elevated; no collapse in U.S. demand.
VIX closed 12.58 on 2018-05-23 after the Feb spike and the March/April tariff scare — markets treating the pause as risk-off relief.
U.S. goods trade deficit narrowed to -$66.567B (May) from -$71.439B (Dec); dispute not yet widening the headline gap.
U.S. goods exports to China down to $10.4B (May) from $13.6B (Dec), a reminder farm/export exposure is real even before 301 tariffs land.

Mnuchin: tariffs on hold while executing the framework; Trump can put tariffs back on if China does not follow through. Lighthizer: purchases significant but forced tech transfer, cyber theft, and innovation protection are far more important; U.S. may still use tariffs, investment restrictions, and export regulations. Joint statement too vague to be binding.

No public $200B deficit-cut commitment. Mnuchin expects 35–40% ag increase this year and energy purchases doubling; Lighthizer: real structural change is necessary. Schumer: a multi-year buy promise without IP/cyber/market-access action would be a loss.

Official text: China will significantly increase purchases; meaningful increases in U.S. agriculture and energy; IP cooperation and China will advance Patent Law amendments; continue high-level talks. No tariff rollback, no dollar target, no ZTE language.

Reports of a possible lift of the ZTE sales ban in exchange for management/board changes and fines; Beijing also offered to remove tariffs on U.S. farm products. Ban remains the sharpest unused non-tariff chip.
